questions.q: Edit: 'One of my friend have gone to Delhi last week.'
questions.a: Two faults — 'friend' → 'friends' (one of + plural) and 'have' → 'has' (head noun 'one' is singular). A wrong answer fixing only one shows single-pass auditing.

questions.q: Edit: 'He discussed about the problem with great details.'
questions.a: 'discussed about' → 'discussed' (discuss takes no preposition) and 'great details' → 'great detail'. A wrong answer changing only 'about' leaves the detail-error.

questions.q: Edit: 'The news are really shocked everyone in the village.'
questions.a: 'are really shocked' → 'really shocked' — 'news' is singular so 'are' is wrong AND 'shocked' needs no auxiliary here, or recast as 'was really shocking'. Either way the 'are' must go.

questions.q: Editing tasks at class 12 run a four-error inventory per passage: tense/form errors, concord errors, determiner errors, and word-form/______ errors — typically one wrong word per line with the correction expected.

Fill in the blank: Editing tasks at class 12 run a four-error inventory per passage: tense/form errors, concord errors, determiner errors, and word-form/______ errors — typically one wrong word per line with the correction expected.
Fill in the blank: The audit ______ per line: (1) verb — right tense for its marker?
Fill in the blank: The audit checklist per line: (______) verb — right tense for its marker?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student locates one error per line in editing passages across the four categories and supplies the correction, naming the governing rule.
